processing: A tea plant cultivar rather than a finished tea, used for black tea among other classes; processing follows whichever class is made.
harvest_season: Probably spring, as is usual; spring one-bud-two-leaf is the sample the source analyses, and no picking calendar is given.
appearance_dry: Depends on the tea made from it; as black tea, typically dark twisted strands.
appearance_liquor: As black tea, typically a clear reddish amber.
appearance_wet: Typically a coppery spent leaf, as with other Chinese black teas.
taste_profile: No tasting description specific to this cultivar is established; as black tea from a leaf this high in polyphenols, expect a firm, brisk cup.

brewing.notes: General settings for a Chinese black tea. Lower the temperature and steep longer if the lot is made as a green tea.

vintage_note: Rarely sold under its own name, since it is a cultivar. Tea made from it follows its class, so buy green as the current spring and black from the current or previous year.
description:
Jianbohuang No. 13 is a Hunan tea cultivar descended from a natural cross of its parent, Jianbohuang. It is the improved child: where the parent is fussy and low-yielding, this one is productive and tough.

Its numbers tell the story. Six-year-old plantings can reach 354 kg per mu, against about 70 kg for the parent. It stands cold well, adapts widely and roots readily from cuttings, so it suits gardens both north and south of the Yangtze.

Spring one-bud-two-leaf material has about 2.4% amino acids, 28% polyphenols, 16.6% total catechins and 4.1% caffeine. That is a brisk, strong profile on paper, and it is valued for black tea. No detailed tasting notes are established.

You are unlikely to see it on a label. If you do, ask which class of tea was made and judge the lot as you would any tea of that class.
history: The Tea Research Institute of the Hunan Academy of Agricultural Sciences bred both this cultivar and its parent. Parent Jianbohuang was selected from the Anhua population between 1957 and 1974; No. 13 came from the natural hybrid seedlings of that plant. The exact date of its release is not well documented.
